title: The LUMA brief
blurb: Your first week at Sprout Lab. Win trust, handle a rival, and deliver for LUMA.

preGame.handoffLine: Your first week at Sprout Lab starts now.

screens.heading: Test an idea about food.
screens.body: Food scientists study how ingredients and processes affect food. Tests help them compare ideas.

screens.heading: Keep records. Know your role.
screens.body: You record and compare. Your mentor guides lab work. Senior staff review the results and decide the next tests.

options.label: A recorded comparison using the same method
options.why: The record shows what was changed and measured.

options.label: A guess based on the nicer package
options.why: The package does not show how the food performed.

preGame.missionLine: Build your skills through new food projects.
preGame.ladderNote: Titles vary by company. Later game projects are not built yet.

endings.headline: Your next assignment is earned.
endings.scoreNote: You earn a place on the next project.
endings.message: Yuki wants you on the next client team. Ren stays your guide, and Imani will be working alongside you.
endings.subline: Level 1 complete. The next chapter is planned, not playable yet.

endings.headline: Revise and retry
endings.message: Ren asks you to try again. Check the brief, use the evidence, and ask for help before the deadline.
endings.subline: Replay Level 1 with what you learned.

endings.headline: This attempt ends here
endings.message: Take a fresh run and use what you learned.
endings.subline: One attempt does not define your future.

scoreTip: Start at 50. Seven scored decisions change reputation by 6. Matching practice does not change your score. Reach 85.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Welcome to Food Science.
beats.body: Your first week at Sprout Lab starts today. Your team builds a drink-trial report for LUMA.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: One week. One place on the next project.
beats.body: LUMA reviews the work Friday. Both juniors want to join the next client team. Your decisions will shape who gets trusted.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.title: Ren has your first assignment.
beats.body: Ren is a senior food scientist. He guides your work and reviews it before it reaches the client.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your work goes through Ren.
beats.body: Follow Ren’s trial sheet and label every sample. He approves changes. Ask him before changing the plan or deciding what goes to the client.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Another junior starts beside you.
beats.body: Imani is working on LUMA too. You exchange a quick hello before the first assignment.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.question: Ren gives you an approved drink-trial plan. What should you do first?

choices.label: Label the samples and follow the trial sheet.
choices.why: Your first job is to carry out and record the approved plan.

choices.label: Change several ingredients to make it exciting.
choices.why: Ren must review changes; extra changes also blur the comparison.

choices.label: Tell LUMA the drink is ready to sell.
choices.why: A junior trial does not approve a product for sale.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.title: Four words for your first assignment.
beats.setup: Ren walks you through the first fruit-drink comparison.

cards.def: A small test of an idea
The thing changed in this trial
A condition kept the same in this trial
A label that links a sample to its record

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.setup: Ren asks you to map the trial sheet before work starts.
beats.question: Match each part of the plan to its job.
beats.whenRight: The plan separates what changes, what stays fixed, and how samples are tracked.
beats.whenWrong: Check each part against the four terms on the trial sheet.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.setup: Ren checks the simple trial plan before you prepare the samples.

items.question: The plan changes only fruit amount. What is the variable?

options.label: Fruit amount.
options.why: That is the factor deliberately changed in this trial.

options.label: The sample code.
options.why: The code identifies the sample; it is not the recipe change.

options.label: The client name.
options.why: The client name is not a trial factor.

items.question: The sheet keeps mixing time the same. What is that condition?

options.label: A constant.
options.why: This trial holds mixing time fixed.

options.label: The variable.
options.why: The planned change is fruit amount, not mixing time.

options.label: A result.
options.why: A fixed condition is part of the method, not a result.

items.question: You record a note about cup 742. What links it to the recipe?

options.label: Its sample code.
options.why: The code joins the cup, recipe record, and note.

options.label: The cup’s position on the table.
options.why: Position can change and is not a reliable record link.

options.label: Which drink looks nicest.
options.why: Appearance does not identify the recipe record.

items.question: This trial changes fruit only. Which extra change would blur the comparison?

options.label: Changing mixing time too.
options.why: Then two recipe conditions differ in a trial meant to compare one.

options.label: Recording both sample codes.
options.why: Codes track the comparison without changing the recipe.

options.label: Using the same mixing time.
options.why: The plan keeps mixing time constant.

beats.whenPass: You can follow the trial plan and keep each sample tied to its record.
beats.whenFail: Separate the planned change, fixed conditions, and sample identity.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.title: Use neutral codes for the tasting.
beats.body: Ren approves codes 318 and 742. Recipe names can shape expectations. Keep the code-to-recipe key with the team; put only the code on each tasting cup.

artifact.title: Recipe labels
artifact.caption: Recipe names before neutral sample codes are applied.
artifact.provenance: Fictional labels; all task facts appear in the question.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Ren approved codes 318 and 742 for this tasting. Which label belongs on a cup?

choices.why: A neutral code identifies the sample without advertising a recipe claim.

choices.label: The sweeter recipe
choices.why: That tells tasters what you expect them to notice.

choices.label: LUMA’s best drink
choices.why: That suggests a preferred answer before the tasting.

beats.speaker: Yuki
beats.title: Yuki arrives for the client review.
beats.body: The R&D Lead needs a clear, accurate report before the client sees it.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Check codes before copying results.
beats.body: Ren’s sheet lists 318 as base and 742 as extra fruit. Each code links notes to a recipe. Copy that link exactly; do not swap the samples.

artifact.title: Coded labels
artifact.caption: LUMA trial samples use neutral codes 318 and 742.
artifact.provenance: Fictional sample codes, not safety or tasting clearance.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Yuki chooses the next client team.
beats.body: Ren reviews your work. Yuki looks for sound judgment and clear evidence before giving you more responsibility.

beats.speaker: Yuki
beats.question: Trial sheet: 318 is base; 742 is extra fruit. Which notebook line is wrong?

choices.label: 742: base recipe.
choices.why: The sheet links 742 to extra fruit. This line assigns it to the wrong recipe.

choices.label: Both codes copied from Ren’s sheet.
choices.why: That describes the record source without changing either recipe link.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

intro.line: Ren and Yuki review your first decisions.

pass.title: You passed the first review.
pass.body: The next client assignment is still yours to earn.

fail.title: You can still turn this around.
fail.body: Use the feedback in the second half.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: The second half of your first week.
beats.body: The report is taking shape. Now the pressure shifts to the team.

beats.speaker: Imani
beats.title: Imani wants that next assignment too.
beats.body: Imani is quick and confident. The client review is a chance to stand out, and sharing credit is not the plan.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The next morning, you hear your work claimed.
beats.body: You wrote the trial notes. Now Imani tells Yuki, “I put that report together.” Your saved file shows your work.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Imani took credit for your report. What should you do?

choices.label: Share the file history with Ren privately.
choices.why: Use the record and the right person without turning it into a public fight.

choices.label: Accuse Imani in front of the client.
choices.why: A client meeting is not the place to settle a team dispute.

choices.label: Post about it online.
choices.why: That exposes private work and makes the conflict public.

choices.label: Change the report to make the rival look bad.
choices.why: Sabotage damages the client’s work and your own trust.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 3:00 P.M. One trial record is incomplete.
beats.body: The fruit amount for 742 is blank. Photos also need tidying. Client review starts at 6:00. Ren must check the missing recipe record.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Sample 742 has no recorded fruit amount. What should you message Ren?

choices.label: Can we leave 742 out until we verify its recipe?
choices.why: A missing recipe prevents a reliable comparison. Ask Ren to review the gap before using it.

choices.label: I’ll guess the amount from its color.
choices.why: Color does not recover the missing recipe record.

choices.label: I’ll use 742 and leave out the missing detail.
choices.why: That hides the gap from the person reviewing the comparison.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 6:00 P.M. The review pack is ready.
beats.body: Ren keeps 742 out of the comparison until its recipe is checked. The review pack states the gap. Photo polish can wait.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Luis still needs a hand.
beats.body: Luis, a lab technician, needs sample labels checked by 6:40. You have finished your work. He owns the final record.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Check labels against the trial sheet.
beats.body: Luis asks you to match each code to the sheet. Set unclear labels aside for him; never fill a gap from memory.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Luis needs sample labels checked. Rank your responses from best to worst.
order: Match codes to the trial sheet; flag unclear labels for Luis.
Leave all the checks for Luis without offering help.
Fill missing codes from memory so the labels look complete.
beats.whenRight: You help with a real lab task and preserve uncertain records for review.
beats.whenWrong: Check the sheet and flag gaps. A complete-looking label is not worth a guessed identity.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Ren noticed how you handled it.
beats.body: Your response under pressure matters, even when the client is not watching.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your first week is complete.
beats.body: Ren sends your work to Yuki. The next assignment depends on the trust you built this week.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: Sprout Lab is choosing the next project team.
beats.body: Your reputation helps decide what happens next.
beats.decidingNote: The team reviews your work and how you handled pressure.
